I will keep my land split so I do not take too much risk. I know wheat-maize best, and with only 6 mu and a family of 4, I want most of the land in the crop rotation I have done for years. So I will put 4 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, because that gives me steady grain and fits my irrigation conditions. I will keep 2 mu for stevia, because it can bring cash, but it needs more careful field work and I do not want to spread myself too thin. I will use improved seed for wheat and stevia, and hybrid seed for maize, because I care most about stable yield on small land. I will fertilize enough to push yield, but not so much that I waste money. Since I have well irrigation, I will water wheat more often, keep maize watered at key stages, and give stevia steady moisture. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat and stevia because it is practical on my small farm, and I will do no-tillage for maize after wheat to save time and catch soil moisture. I will spray only as much as I think is needed to keep weeds, insects, and disease from cutting yield.
